answers.M8-S1: The author caught forty Mason-bees, marked them, and let them go two and a half miles from home, and some of them flew back to the nest.
answers.M8-S2: Because a stiff breeze came up and made things harder for the bees, so they had to fly close to the ground.
answers.M8-S3: They had a load of pollen under their bellies when they got back at twenty minutes to three.
answers.M8-S4: He had to mark them with chalk and gum arabic before setting them free, and it was hard because he got stung.
answers.M8-S5: When he got home he hardly thought the bees would be there, but then Aglaé told him two had arrived.
answers.M8-S6: It tells about the experiment in order: catching the bees, marking and releasing them, the wind, then coming home.
answers.M8-S7: To show the bees flew two and a half miles in less than three quarters of an hour.
answers.M8-S8: Because he squeezed some of them too hard and got stung while marking them, so about twenty got hurt.
answers.M8-S9: That they had to fly close to the ground because of the wind.
